links.outcome: Physician vignette performance with versus without LLM access, and usage-related gains
links.effect: LLM access improved performance: Kenya 18% (95% CI 12.7-23.2), Indonesia 10.7% (5.7-15.7), Netherlands 7.2% (3.7-10.7); some control physicians outperformed those with access.
links.quote: Higher LLM usage was associated with greater performance gains, though some physicians without access outperformed those with access, suggesting that effective use depends on individual engagement.

links.outcome: Distribution of LLM performance benefits across countries and within-country score dispersion
links.effect: LLM access reduced cross-country performance disparities, particularly Kenya vs Netherlands; score dispersion increased in Indonesia and decreased in Kenya.
links.quote: However, distributional effects varied, with increased score dispersion in Indonesia and reduced variation in Kenya.

screen.reason: Multi-country randomized controlled trial evaluating the impact of providing clinicians with access to an LLM (GPT-4o) during standardized clinical vignette evaluations.
